title: Model/config snapshot diff + augmented smoke tests for incident-driven eval regressions
creator: Siona Patel
description: Summary: After a recent production incident where a seemingly minor tokenizer/config change triggered a measurable quality regression on a customer-facing rerank flow, we discovered gaps in our eval coverage for cross-config diffs. This ticket implements a deterministic snapshot->diff->augmented-smoke pipeline: take model+config snapshots at deploy time, compute diffs vs previous snapshot, and automatically run an adaptive set of smoke evals weighted by diff type and expected signal. The aim is to 1) catch regressions earlier in deploy pipelines, 2) generate targeted postmortem artifacts automatically, and 3) encode learnings into long-running regression tests.
investigation_summary: On 2025-02-24 a canary rollout of runtime-1.18 included a tokenizer update and a batching tweak. Observability flagged a 3% drop in rerank precision for a high-value customer. Post-incident traceback showed that the new tokenizer altered tokenization boundaries for our golden prompts; the change was not covered by smoke evals because the existing tests compare model outputs between versions but do not prioritize tokenizer or prefix-kv changes. We reproduced locally by replaying the exact request stream and confirmed the regression across two model variants.
root_cause: Insufficient mapping between config changes (tokenizer, kv-ttl, batch-schedule) and targeted eval suites. The deploy pipeline only executes a flat set of smoke tests that treat all config changes equally, so low-signal but high-impact diffs (tokenizer boundary shifts) were mis-prioritized.
mitigations_applied: 1) Rolled back tokenizer config in the canary. 2) Added temporary alert rule to surface rerank precision drops >= 1.5% in canaries. 3) Cross-team blameless postmortem and immediate addition of replayed traces to eval artifacts. These stopgap measures prevent recurrence while we build the snapshot-diff pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
- On any deploy, a model+config snapshot is produced and stored in S3 with metadata (model-tag, config-hash, deploy-id, commit).
- Diff engine computes granular deltas: tokenizer changes, kv-cache param changes, quantization profile differences, batching/kernel selections.
- Diff-to-test mapper selects an ordered smoke test set with weights; critical diffs trigger high-weight tests that run in CI/canary.
- Failure of a high-weight test blocks canary promotion and surfaces an automatic incident artifact (replay + diff report + failing prompts).
- Post-deploy dashboard displays snapshot history and recent diffs for last 30 deploys.
implementation_plan:
1) Define snapshot schema (model metadata, config files, artifact hashes) and a compact JSON representation (team sync 2025-03-03).
2) Build lightweight snapshot writer in deploy pipeline (CI hook + runtime sidecar) — target 0.5 engineer-weeks for prototype.
3) Implement diff engine: token-level tokenizer comparator, kv/ttl numeric comparator, quantization metadata comparator. Prioritize tokenizer comparator first.
4) Implement diff->test mapping rules (initial heuristic ruleset stored in repo; later ML-based scoring).
5) Integrate with smoke eval runner: allow weighted tests, early exit on critical fails, generate replay & artifact bundle on fail.
6) Add dashboard hooks and alerting rules.
7) Run canary with synthetic and live traffic for two weeks and iterate.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for snapshot writer and diff engine.
- Regression tests that inject synthetic tokenizer changes and assert the diff engine selects tokenizer-focused smoke tests.
- End-to-end CI run that simulates a deploy with a controlled diff and verifies canary is blocked when high-weight tests fail.
- Backfill: run new smoke suite against last 10 production snapshots to surface latent issues and calibrate weights.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): snapshot writing + tokenizer diff + mapped smoke tests in canary only (2 weeks). Phase 2 (CI): enable snapshot diffs in PR CI and fail fast for critical diffs (follow-up week). Phase 3 (prod): enable artifact generation and dashboarding across all deploys. Each phase gated by metrics: false positive rate of blockers < 10% and detection rate of historical incidents >= 80%.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New metric: diff_count_by_type and weighted_smoke_failures_by_deploy.
- Alert: weighted_smoke_failures_in_canary >=1 -> pager to oncall.
- Dashboard panels: snapshot lineage, recent diffs heatmap, canary smoke pass rate.
notes_and_links: S3 prefix for prototype snapshots: s3://redwood-eval-snapshots/proto/
